title: Damayanti
hook: a husband has vanished, and Damayanti sends out not soldiers but a question

segments.voice: Yesterday, Damayanti in the hall of five faces, choosing the one with dust and a shadow.

How do you find someone who doesn't want to be found? Damayanti's husband lost everything at dice, walked into the forest with her, cut their one shared cloth while she slept, and left. She survived the forest and made her way home to her father's house in Vidarbha, to her children. Nala is out there somewhere, changed, hidden, ashamed. A king's daughter could send riders. Damayanti sends something smaller and sharper. Her second choice: how to search.
screen: `HE DOESN'T WANT TO BE FOUND.` → `HOME IN VIDARBHA.` → `HER SECOND CHOICE.`

segments.voice: She calls Brahmanas, travelers who go from court to court, and gives them a question to repeat wherever people gather. In paraphrase: where have you gone, gambler, after cutting half the cloth of the wife who loved you and leaving her asleep in the forest? She's still waiting, wearing half a cloth. Have mercy, and answer. Don't say who sent you, she adds. If anyone answers, notice who he is and where he lives, and bring me his words. Look at how the question is built. It isn't an accusation shouted in a square. It names only things two people would know: a gambler, a cut cloth, a sleeping wife. A stranger hears a riddle. The one man it's meant for hears his own story. And it asks him to answer, which leaves him room to speak instead of run. Then a messenger, in a far city, reports back. A plain charioteer heard the words and answered with a strange defense of a husband who had even lost his cloth to the birds. Nobody but Nala would know that detail. Damayanti doesn't rush. She tells her mother and asks that her father not be told yet. Then she sets a careful trap: word goes out that she'll choose a husband again, tomorrow, so soon that only a driver with Nala's skill could bring a king there in time. When the chariot arrives, she sends her maid Keshini to watch the charioteer. Then she sends their children to him, and she watches him weep. Only then does she let him in. She doesn't trust rumor. She tests with love.
screen: `ONE QUESTION, CARRIED FAR` · `ONLY HE WOULD KNOW THE ANSWER` · `A CHARIOTEER ANSWERS` · `SHE TESTS BEFORE SHE TRUSTS`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who has gone quiet on you, a friend, a sibling, someone you've lost touch with. Don't rehearse what went wrong; let one small, kind question come to mind that only the two of you would understand, and hold the question, not the answer. If you pray, you can hold that person in prayer.
Damayanti. The wife who searched with a question only her husband could answer, and tested before she trusted.
Your line: Damayanti. A question can carry what an accusation can't. I'll be here tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus know Damayanti's search from the Mahabharata's forest book, where Brihadashva tells it to the exiled Yudhishthira; it is also retold in later poems, plays and dance.

chat.says: Why didn't Damayanti just send soldiers to drag Nala home?
options: She sent a gentle question only he'd understand, so he had room to answer instead of run.
She had no way to send anyone, since her father refused to help her search.
She didn't really want him back, so she searched only to prove he'd left.
chat.meaning: Her question named only what two people knew, a gambler, a cut cloth, a sleeping wife, and asked him to answer.
